sentences.text: The Respondent No.3 in O.P.(M.V.) No.1138/2008 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Thrissur, is the appellant herein.
The petitioners in the OP are the Cross Objectors in CO.No.131/2019 (For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).

2. The O.P. was filed under under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, by the parents of the deceased minor child by name Firoz, who died in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 08.10.2007.

According to them, on 08.10.2007, at about 5.40 a.m., while the deceased was standing by the side of the road, a car bearing reg.no.KL 08/AK/1616 driven by the 2 nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner, knocked him down and as a result of which he sustained serious injuries and later on he succumbed to the injuries, on 10.10.2007.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the 2025:KER:30852 MACA NO.2105 OF 2018 & CO NO.131 OF 2019 offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. was Rs.10,61,000/- limited to Rs.8,00,000/-.
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A9, B1 and B2.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.7,30,750/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the Respondent No.3 preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
9. Heard Sri.T.C.Suresh Menon, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners/appellants, and Sri.P.Jacob Mathew, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.

. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
11.
The Tribunal has taken the notional income of the child at Rs.4000/- and applied multiplier 15 for the purpose of assessing the loss of dependency.
In addition to the same, a sum of Rs.1 lakh was Reliance General Insurance Company vs Mohammed Yasi on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39796447/

3 awarded on the head 'loss of love and affection', Rs.30000/- was awarded on the head 'loss of estate', Rs.50000/- was awarded on the head 'shortened expectancy of life and another Rs.25000/-
was awarded on the head 'funeral expenses'.
According to the learned counsel for the appellant, the compensation awarded on the above heads are on the higher side.

On the other hand, according to the learned counsel for the petitioner the notional income of the deceased child fixed by the Tribunal at Rs.4000/- is on the lower side and the learned counsel would argue that the notional income of the child is to be fixed at least as that of a coolie as fixed by the apex court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236].

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He has also contended that the multiplier that is to be applied is 20 and not 15.
12.

In the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v. Assainar 2025:KER:30852 MACA NO.2105 OF 2018 & CO NO.131 OF 2019 [ 2019(4) KLT 39], a learned Single Judge of this Court after referring to other important decisions on the point formulated a schedule for fixing the notional income of deceased children within the age group of 6-15.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd v. Assainar 2025:KER:30852 MACA NO.2105 OF 2018 & CO NO.131 OF 2019 [ 2019(4) KLT 39]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the above schedule, the notional annual income of a child within the above age group during the year 2007-2008 will come to Rs.47,000/-.
As per the above decision the multiplier to be applied is 15 and 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expense.
Therefore, the loss of dependency as per the above decision will come to only Rs.4,70,000/-.
However in the instant case, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.4,80,000/- on the head loss of dependency.

13. In the decision in Meena Devi vs. Nunu Chand Mahto @ Nemchand Mahto and others [AIR 2022 SC 5006], in the case of a 12 year old child involved in the accident in the year 2003, the notional annual income taken was only Rs.30,000/- and the multiplier applied was 15.

entities.text: Meena Devi vs. Nunu Chand Mahto @ Nemchand Mahto and others [AIR 2022 SC 5006]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The total compensation awarded by the apex court was only Rs.5,00,000/-.

In the decision in Kusmi Devi vs.
M.D. Kasim and Others [MANU/SC/1124/2023], in the case of a 3 year old child involved in an accident in the year 1994 also the notional annual income taken was 2025:KER:30852 MACA NO.2105 OF 2018 & CO NO.131 OF 2019 Rs.30,000/- and the multiplier applied was 15.

entities.text:
Kusmi Devi vs.
M.D. Kasim and Others [MANU/SC/1124/2023]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Though the High Court was awarded only a total sum of Rs.5,00,000/-, the apex court has enhanced the total compensation to Rs.6,00,000/- by adding Rs.1,00,000/- on the head 'global compensation'.
14.

Going by the decision in Assainar (supra) in addition to the loss of dependency, the petitioners are entitled to get compensation on conventional heads as decided by the apex court in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, they are entitled to get a consolidated sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses, and the dependents (parents, children and spouse) are entitled to get a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium, with an increase of 10% in every three years.
Therefore, towards loss of estate and funeral expense they are entitled to get a sum of Rs.18,150/- each.

Towards loss of consortium,
petitioners together are entitled to get a sum of Rs.96800/- (48,400 x 2).

15. Since compensation for loss of consortium was given, further compensation for love and affection cannot be granted, in view of the decision in New India Assurance Company Ltd. v.
Somwati and Others, 2025:KER:30852 MACA NO.2105 OF 2018 & CO NO.131 OF 2019 (2020)9 SCC 644.

The deceased died in this case died 2 days after the accident.

In the above circumstances, I hold that the compensation awarded towards pain and suffering is on the lower side, and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.30000/-.
17.
